chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from 'Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Yunus, from Mu'awiyah ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I said to Abī 'Abdillāh عليه السلام: When I stand for salat (prayer), do I recite “In the Name of Allah, the All-beneficent, the All-merciful” in Fātiḥat al-Kitāb? He said: Yes. I said: Then when I have recited Fātiḥat al-Kitāb, do I recite “In the Name of Allah, the All-beneficent, the All-merciful” along with the surah? He said: Yes.

key_terms.السُّورَةِ: the additional Qur'anic chapter recited after Fātiḥat al-Kitāb
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the ritual worship being discussed
key_terms.بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ: the basmalah formula recited at the beginning of the surahs
key_terms.فَاتِحَةِ الْكِتَابِ: Sūrat al-Ḥamd, the opening chapter recited in salat (prayer)
key_terms.نَعَمْ: an affirmative response indicating permissibility and prescription

ai.seo_question: Should بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ be recited in both Fātiḥat al-Kitāb and the following surah during salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith states that بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ is to be recited in Fātiḥat al-Kitāb and also with the surah recited after it in salat (prayer). It serves as a jurisprudential proof for the recitation of the basmalah as part of Qur'anic recitation within prayer.
